title: 1M advertised context vs. a 256K compaction clamp in the shipped binaries, plus quota and `agy -p` policy questions (Desktop 2.29.0 / CLI 1.5.1)

posts.name: A Feng
posts.cooked:
We have filed a bug report on the official repository and published an archive that documents where Google Antigravity’s published specifications and terms differ from the shipped client (Desktop v2.29.0, CLI v1.5.1, as of Nov 5, 2026).

  • GitHub issue: [Bug]: Auto-compaction is clamped to 256,000 tokens (0x3E800) on models advertised and displayed with a 1,048,576-token window (v1.5.1) · Issue #1432 · google-antigravity/antigravity-cli · GitHub
  • Evidence archive: GitHub - magiccodelab/antigravity-256k-context-discrepancy: Evidence archive: Google Antigravity advertises a 1M-token context window but hardcodes auto-compaction at 256K (0x3E800), plus the agy -p headless policy reversal. · GitHub

Additional copies (copy-paste; new accounts are limited to 2 links per post):

https://github.com/magiccodelab/antigravity-256k-context-discrepancy/blob/main/antigravity-256k-report.md

1. 1,048,576 tokens advertised, 256,000 enforced

Gemini 4 Argon is registered in the client with a 0x100000 (1,048,576) token window, and the documentation and the /context view present it as a ~1M window. In the official binaries, cortex/utils/utils.GetCheckpointConfig contains:

cmp $0x3e800,%edx; mov $0x3e800,%esi; cmovb %edx,%esi

This caps the auto-compaction threshold at min(calculated, 256,000) tokens, about 25% of the advertised window, for every model. The sequence occurs once in .text at file offset 0x7fb0fe2 in CLI 1.5.1, 0x7fe5802 in CLI 1.5.0, and 0x176cca2 in Desktop 2.29.0 language_server.exe. All binaries were downloaded from storage.googleapis.com, and their hashes are listed in the issue.

2. Session data matches the binary

  • 15,575 model calls recorded across 209 local CLI 1M-Gemini sessions all carry max_context_tokens = 256000, and no single-attempt call exceeded 300K tokens.
  • An independent audit in #878 (310 sessions, 65,613 calls) measured a maximum single-call input of 255,999 tokens and no calls above 300K.
  • Each compaction stalls the session for a median of 70 seconds, does not record the summary call’s token usage in gen_metadata, and discards the 240K+ implicit prompt cache.

3. Current official position

In #198191 (Nov 4), Google staff stated that the ~250K threshold “is a fixed default and isn’t user-configurable yet” and handled the report as a feature request. We consider this a specification issue. The product advertises and displays 1,048,576 tokens, while the binary enforces 256,000 without disclosure.

The binary also contains 512K (about 1.3x quota per turn) and 900K (1.8x, Expensive: true) context options. They are gated behind a whitelist with a single entry, “Gemini 4 Argon”.

4. Quota

A community A/B test in #196351, run within the same quota bucket, measured Gemini 4 Argon drawing subscription quota at about 3x the rate of Gemini 3.8 Flash per dollar of published API price. Gemini web pure-input tests measured 7.64x–9.25x. In that thread, Google staff replied that published API prices are promotional pay-as-you-go rates and that internal subscription quota multipliers are not published.

5. agy -p policy

  • Between Sep 16 and Oct 8, the forum received 10 written confirmations that running the unmodified agy -p binary as a local subprocess from tools such as Codex or Claude Code complied with Section 6 of the Additional Terms: #175905, #183429, #185494, #185460, #185992, #185949, #186954, #186952, #186246, #187536.
  • On Oct 8, 71 minutes after the last of these, a reply in #187241 reversed that position and warned of automated account suspension.
  • In #191689 (post #8), Google staff confirmed that the Terms of Service had not been modified after September, and that only the FAQ had been updated in mid-October.

The support engineers who answered those threads applied Section 6 as written and as the --output-format json / stream-json interface suggests. We do not hold them responsible for the later change. The questions below are for the teams that own product limits, quota, and policy.

What we are asking for

  1. Remove the 256,000 clamp so that 1M models compact near their computed threshold. If 256K is an intended product limit, state it in the documentation and model listings, and show the real threshold in /context.
  2. Publish the per-model subscription quota multipliers.
  3. State whether the Additional Terms or the FAQ governs agy -p subprocess use. If the policy has changed, amend the Terms and notify subscribers.

All download URLs, SHA-256/SHA-512 hashes, disassembly listings, and forum snapshots are in the archive for independent verification.

posts.name: Rebbanpalli Naveen
posts.cooked:
HI @A_Feng,

Welcome to the Forum.

Thank you for the detailed feedback across all three topics. Here is how each item currently works:

  1. ~256K Auto-Compaction Threshold: In Antigravity App (2.29.0) and Antigravity CLI (1.5.1), automatic context compaction triggers by default around ~250K–256K tokens to maintain latency, reliability, and token efficiency, and is not currently user-configurable. We have shared your feedback requesting a configurable compaction threshold and clearer trigger indicators in /context with our engineering team.
  2. Subscription Quota Multipliers: As noted in the Plans documentation, subscription quota consumption correlates with the complexity and volume of agent work and adjusts dynamically based on system capacity, so fixed per-model multipliers are not published.
  3. Using agy -p in Third-Party Agents: The Google Antigravity Terms of Service (Section 6) and Official FAQ apply together: Headless mode (agy -p) is supported for your own direct scripting and CI/CD pipelines, whereas wrapping agy inside third-party coding agents is not permitted under consumer plans (use a pay-as-you-go Gemini API key or Gemini Enterprise instead).

posts.name: A Feng
posts.cooked:
Thanks for the reply. I’ll keep this to the context threshold.

1. “Default” does not describe what ships. A default is something a user can change. In App 2.29.0 and CLI 1.5.1, GetCheckpointConfig takes whatever threshold it computes and applies min(value, 256000) (cmp $0x3e800; cmovb). Nothing a user can set gets past that line: AGY_CLI_AUTO_COMPACT_OVERRIDE values above 256,000 are overwritten by the same instruction, and its percentage form always evaluates to 0. A limit that nothing can raise is the effective context window, and today that number is 256,000, not 1,048,576.

2. The stated reason changed in two days. On Nov 5 in #1432 it was “multi-step reasoning quality, turn latency, and per-turn quota consumption.” Today it is “latency, reliability, and token efficiency.” Both are reasonable product goals. Neither explains why the model listing, the docs, and /context still say 1M.

3. Early compaction has its own costs on those same axes. Google staff said so in #198191: “compacting this early costs both cache efficiency and detail.” Logs in #1291 show each compaction pausing the session for a median of 70 seconds, discarding a 240K+ cached prefix, and leaving the summary call’s tokens out of usage records. That is a trade-off, and users pay for it, so users should be told about it.

4. The cost concern already has an answer in the product. The binary ships 512K (1.3x quota) and 900K (1.8x, Expensive: true) options, restricted to a whitelist with a single entry. Keeping them off is a product decision, which is fine, but it is not a latency or reliability limit.

5. My request was restated. I did not mainly ask for a configurable threshold. I asked that, if 256K is the intended limit, the documentation, the model listings, and /context say so. That is a documentation change, not an engineering project.

Four questions, each answerable with yes, no, or a date:

  1. In App 2.29.0 and CLI 1.5.1, is there any supported setting that lets a session exceed 256,000 tokens before compaction?
  2. Which public page tells a subscriber, before purchase, that a model listed at 1M compacts at 256K?
  3. Which of the two stated reasons is the official one?
  4. Will the docs, model listings, and /context be corrected to show 256,000, and in which release?
